source_summary: Queried 4 GitHub Search API surfaces saved under /tmp/radar_2026_10_04_api/ for recently created or pushed repositories around AI agents, MCP, LLM apps, browser/computer-use, code agents, workflow, RAG, assistant, copilot, memory, and skills. Deduplicated more than 140 visible candidates from the returned pages. Repository/readme audit first used GitHub repository/readme APIs, then switched to raw.githubusercontent.com README fetches after unauthenticated GitHub API returned 403 rate limits; selected raw READMEs were saved under /tmp/radar_2026_10_04_readmes/. No third-party repository was cloned.
trend_observations: Today the strongest AI-native product signal is agent operations becoming visible and stateful: multi-agent teams, cross-agent model routers, local memory stores, token/context middleware, visual artifact canvases, remote sandboxes, approval cards, and bug queues that agents can claim. The product frontier is less about another chatbot shell and more about durable surfaces around agency: roles, permissions, receipts, context ownership, schedules, and human review points.
assumptions: Scores are based on GitHub Search metadata, raw README evidence, root-content evidence where available, stars/forks/created_at/pushed_at, install/release/demo/docs/test/security signals, and clarity of user workflow. GitHub unauthenticated repo/readme API hit 403 during shortlist audit, so later candidates use search metadata plus raw README evidence rather than full root-content API evidence. No third-party repository was cloned, installed, built, run, browser-tested, desktop-tested, mobile-tested, MCP-connected, credential-tested, provider-tested, security-tested, payment-tested, or deployed locally. Star counts and pushed_at values are point-in-time snapshots from the discovery window.
markdown_report: See data/runs/2026-10-04.md for the complete human-readable report. Top themes: persistent multi-agent teams, cross-agent model routing, self-hosted agent runtimes, portable local memory, token/context middleware, agent-native media creation, visual artifact canvases, remote coding pods, agent-ready bug queues, and scheduled approval-gated personal agents.

top_projects.summary: Open-source CLI/TUI system for defining Claude Code, Codex, and Pi agent teams in YAML, then running persistent owner/checker seats against a repository.
top_projects.audience: Developers and small teams coordinating multiple coding agents inside real repositories.
top_projects.ai_native_angle: Turns separate terminal agents into a named, stateful team with roles, shared context, queues, dashboards, provider hooks, and review flow.
top_projects.growth_signal: Pushed 2026-10-04 with about 4,697 stars. Search metadata plus raw README show npm CLI, tmux/Codex/Claude setup, TUI GIF, first-project rigs, dry-run setup, trust/permission documentation, security/community files, and release/npm badges.
top_projects.runnability: High from npm package, guided first-use path, CLI/TUI commands, docs, and explicit machine-change disclosure; not installed or run locally.
top_projects.recommended_action: Run `rig setup --dry-run` in a disposable repo, then test one owner/checker change and inspect queue, review artifact, and permission writes.

top_projects.summary: Local SQLite and Markdown memory layer for coding agents that can mark facts wrong, supersede old facts, recall via BM25/MCP, and wire into Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, OpenClaw, and Pi.

top_projects.ai_native_angle: Treats memory as mutable evidence with wrong/superseded ranking, provenance, hooks, and cross-agent recall rather than static notes.
top_projects.growth_signal: Pushed 2026-10-04 with about 770 stars. README shows npm package, CI, benchmark receipts, zero runtime deps, MCP server, Codex hooks, Markdown mirrors, importers, daily job, and security/data notes.
top_projects.runnability: High from package, CLI commands, documented hooks, tests/benchmarks, and local storage model; no hooks, MCP server, or recall benchmark was run.
top_projects.recommended_action: Initialize in a toy repo and test wrong-memory demotion, supersede flow, Codex hook trust, and Markdown mirror review.
